messages:
danielle: Quick idea — propose we add a lightweight 'affinity shards' layer to routing to reduce cross-region tail latency for heavy tenants. Basic idea: map a tenant to 2-3 region-affinitized shards, prefer those pools for low-latency, fallback to global pool when saturated. sketch config:
```
affinity_shards: 3
sticky_ttl: 5m
fallback: global_low_cost
```
Would love rapid ops/security/arch feedback on failure modes and rollout approach.

shiv: Nice pattern. Main concern is state growth — per-tenant sticky maps can blow up. How do we GC/limit entries?

danielle: Plan A: deterministic mapping + optional short-lived sticky cache. GC via TTL+LRU; only create shards for high-traffic tenants (default shards=0).

leo: Two tradeoffs to highlight: (1) shards reduce tail by keeping hot flows co-located, (2) they reduce multiplexing so GPU utilization might drop. Need simulation. Also how do we derive affinity score? latency p95 vs cost?

kate: Ops question: during deploys/restarts we must avoid massive reshuffle. Prefer deterministic consistent-hash mapping with a seed/version so changes are explicit. Also how do we increase shard count safely?

danielle: Agreed re: deterministic mapping. Implementation thought: shard = hash(tenant_id, mapping_version) % shard_count. That avoids central sticky state; we can add a small local sticky cache for multi-request burst affinity. For changing shard_count we bump mapping_version and add a migration window where both mappings accepted.

shiv: That helps state size. Still need capacity controls per-shard (hot tenants can still swamp a shard). We need admission/overflow policies.

leo: Overflow options: queue (adds latency), reject (429), or overflow to global pool (higher cost). I prefer overflow -> global pool with a cost penalty + backpressure signal so clients can adapt.

kate: Observability: we need metrics per-tenant-per-shard: shard_util, tenant_shard_hits, overflow_rate, remapped_count. Dashboards + 1 alert if overflow_rate > 1% for >5m.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for routing-service/v2 -> prod-az1 at 2026-02-10T18:43:12Z :rocket:

danielle: Open questions for the RFC: alpha/beta weights for scoring, shard_count defaults and heuristics, migration + rollback checklist. Proposal: default shards=0, enable per-tenant when 95th percentile TPS > 5r/s, default shards=2 for enabled tenants. Thoughts?

shiv: ACK on thresholds but make everything configurable per-tenant (account API + admin UI). Some customers will want stricter guarantees.

leo: Add a mandatory sim step in the PR: offline trace replay to estimate delta in tail vs GPU idle. If cost increases >10% for <20% tail improvement, gate it.

kate: I'll volunteer to stub dashboards and the alerting rules. Also we should include a small runbook for migration failures (how to flip mapping_version back, how to drain shards).

danielle: Great. I'll open the RFC with the deterministic mapping, overflow->global default, and sim requirements. Will include checklist for staging -> canary -> prod and the rollback commands. Thanks all :+1:

leo: one more nit — add a tenant opt-out flag for compliance-sensitive customers that require global routing.

danielle: noted, add opt-out flag to account settings and API.

kate: LGTM. Ping me when RFC lands and I'll hook dashboards to the metrics pipeline.

shiv: I'll draft the admission controller sketch (throttles + signals) and share in the RFC thread.

danielle: cool — RFC incoming within the day.
